questions.q: What does a model inversion attack reconstruct?
options: Representative features of the training inputs that produced a model's outputs, using only those outputs or confidence scores
A full copy of the model's weights file
The model's source code and training script
The physical server infrastructure the model runs on
questions.explain: Model inversion uses a model's outputs, confidence scores, or gradients to reconstruct representative features of the inputs that produced them, without direct access to training data.

questions.q: In Fredrikson et al.'s 2015 model inversion research, what did they demonstrate against a facial recognition API?
options: They proved confidence scores have no effect on inversion attack success
They reconstructed a recognizable face image for a given name using only the model's own outputs, repeatedly queried
They extracted the model's full training dataset directly from its database
They showed model inversion is impossible against any real-world deployed model
questions.explain: Fredrikson et al. reconstructed a recognizable face image for a given identity using only the facial recognition API's predicted identity and confidence score as the optimization signal.

questions.q: What question does a membership inference attack answer?
options: What is the model's exact architecture?
How many total records exist in the training set?
What company trained the model?
Was a specific record part of this model's training set — yes or no?
questions.explain: Membership inference, formalized by Shokri et al. (2017), determines whether a given record was part of a model's training data by exploiting differences in model confidence.

questions.q: What underlying mechanism makes membership inference attacks work?
options: Overfitting — a model tends to be more confident on data it has memorized than on unseen data from the same distribution
The attacker must already have physical access to the training database
All models are equally confident on every input, with no learnable pattern
Membership inference requires the victim to publish their training data publicly first
questions.explain: Shokri et al. showed that a model which has memorized training data even slightly is measurably more confident on records it trained on than on similar unseen records — that confidence gap is what shadow models learn to detect.

questions.q: Why can membership inference be a serious privacy violation even when the model's prediction task seems unrelated to the sensitive fact being leaked?
options: It can't be — membership inference only ever reveals information already in the model's stated prediction

Determining someone's record was in a training set for a specific sensitive study (e.g. an HIV-status or cancer study) discloses their participation in that study, independent of the model's actual task
Membership inference only works on models with zero accuracy
It requires the attacker to already know the person's full medical history
questions.explain: If a model was trained on a sensitive cohort, confirming a named individual's membership in that training set discloses their participation in that cohort by itself, regardless of what the model predicts.
